scenario: A salary benchmarking firm collects data from a professional networking platform where users only report salaries above $60,000 (the platform's minimum for 'professional' listing). An HR consultant uses the platform's average to advise clients on market rates.

data.description: Platform only lists salaries > $60,000. Underlying salary distribution assumed Normal with known standard deviation Ïƒ = $25,000.

question: The platform reports a mean salary of $85,000. Using the truncated normal model, estimate (a) the true mean salary Î¼ across the full labour market (including unlisted roles), and (b) the fraction of roles that appear on the platform.
naive_answer: The true mean salary is approximately $85,000 since that is the platform average.
naive_trap: About 32% of market salaries are below $60,000 and invisible to the platform. The true market mean is about $13,000 lower than the platform figure. An HR consultant quoting $85,000 as a market benchmark would systematically overprice talent or underpay relative to expectations.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(60000-mu)/25000; sf=norm.sf(a); return mu+25000*norm.pdf(a)/sf-85000 if sf>1e-10 else 1e10
mu=brentq(eq,1000,84999)
assert abs(mu-72026)<600
assert abs(norm.sf((60000-mu)/25000)-0.6848)<0.01
